newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour wants full disclosure from US REC owners.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour wants full disclosure from US REC owners.

text.p: Britain's main opposition Labour party said on Wednesday it would examine ways of ensuring that U.S. firms that take over regional electricity companies (RECs) fully disclose the subsidiaries' profits.

Commenting on the 1.3 billion pound cash bid for East Midlands Electricity Plc by U.S. energy utility Dominion Resources Inc, energy spokesman John Battle said Labour had no opposition in principle to overseas takeovers.

But he added: "I believe it is wrong that the companies which have been taken over are no longer required to issue individual reports demonstrating the level of profits they have made in the UK, and I will urgently review options to see how this information can be made available to the public."
Nine of the 12 RECs in England and Wales have now been taken over or are the subject of a bid. Five of the nine bidders are American.
"It is absolutely vital that these industries do not move beyond the reach of the regulator. U.S.-owned companies must face regulation on a par with U.K.-owned companies," Battle said in a statement.
Labour officials said they were not considering requiring additional information but were concerned to ensure that figures disclosed to the regulators were also freely available to the public.
Battle said a Labour government would not be a "soft touch" once Britain's electricity industry is fully opened to competition in 1998.

"Labour will promote competition where possible and has plans for tough, efficient regulation wherever necessary in the privatised utilities and we intend to see it enforced whoever is the owner," he said.
